title: Independently check #4554's paid phase and exp tables: own tables vs 16(E+d)/Q and 2^-p, worst-direction seeds (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/pr4554-native-tables-check/`, an independent check of the paid native tables in Dugongue's #4554 (head `4f46c6a9`): the root powers `z^e` (`PHASE-TABLES.md` §1) and `exp(−x)` (`NATIVE-EXP-TABLE.md`). It follows my #4556, #4557 and #4558 on the same PR. **All checked claims are confirmed. No new κ.**

The texts are vendored (blobs `2dab8f3e` and `ee6e734c`, SHA256-pinned). Nothing is imported from #4554's table code.

## Checks

- **Root-power tables.** My own implementation of the squarings, digit tables and queries, with nearest rounding to `1/Q` at the smallest `Q ≥ 64(E+d)`.
  - **Query error.** Six `(D, t)` pairs up to `D = 2^20`, each with all four worst-direction grid seeds (error `< 1/Q`). All 20,852 queries are within `16(E+d)/Q` of a decimal reference (AGM π); the worst is 0.076 of the bound.
  - **Magnitudes.** Coordinates, products and sums stay within `2Q`, `4Q²` and `8Q²`.
  - **Factor count.** A literal tree unfolding confirms the `2E+d` error-factor count.
- **Exp table.** Constants `(c, C, η, d, c0) = (1, 2, 1/4, 13, 6)` satisfy `η(d+1) > c+η+2`, at `n = 2^16`, `2^20` and `2^24`.
  - **Taylor base.** It satisfies `0 ≤ q̂ ≤ e^(−h)` with `C_d ≤ 0.96`.
  - **Table entries.** Every entry satisfies `0 ≤ e^(−jh) − Ê_j ≤ j(C_d+1)2^(−S)`; the worst is 0.70 of the bound.
  - **Queries.** 612 queries all have error `< 2^−p`.
  - **Cutoff.** The tail condition holds for every `2 ≤ log₂(n+2) ≤ 4096`, so no cutoff is needed for these constants.
  - **Signed corollary.** The reciprocal `exp(+x)` meets `< 2^−p`.
- **Binding.** 10 statements are bound verbatim to the vendored texts.

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr4554-native-tables-check
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/pr4554-native-tables-check outcome=completed   (seconds, stdlib only)
```

**Limitations:**
- `PHASE-TABLES.md` §2 (linear-program lowering) is out of scope.
- The exp table is checked for one constant set and three sizes.
- References are high-precision decimal, not interval-certified.
